seo.metaTitle: Facebook Hashtag Generator: Honest About What Works
seo.metaDescription: Generate Facebook hashtags and find out why two or three is the limit worth using. Free tool with no login and no uploads.

intro: It is worth saying plainly: hashtags do very little on Facebook. People do not browse hashtag pages there the way they do on Instagram, and Facebook's distribution is driven by what your friends and groups engage with rather than by subject tags. Two or three relevant ones will not hurt and occasionally help with local or community terms. A block of twenty will do nothing except make the post look like it was copied from Instagram. This generator gives you a small honest set, and spends more of its effort telling you where the actual levers are.
howto: Describe your post in a few plain words.
Check the topic it matched and adjust if needed.
Leave the count at two. Three at the most.
Press Build and drop anything that is not genuinely about your post.
Paste them at the end of the post, after the text that is doing the real work.
benefits: The value here is partly in what it refuses to do. A tool that hands you thirty Facebook hashtags is either not paying attention or hoping you will not notice, and copying an Instagram caption wholesale onto Facebook is one of the most visible signs of an account posting everywhere without thinking. Keeping it to two or three keeps the post looking native to the platform.

It also points at what does work, which is more useful than the tags themselves. On Facebook the first line of your text decides whether anyone expands the post, sharing into relevant groups reaches people no tag will, and a post that gets comments early travels further than one that gets likes. None of that is about hashtags, and a hashtag tool that says so is being straight with you.
useCases: Local businesses get the most out of Facebook hashtags, because location and community terms are the one area where they still do a little work. Event pages and community groups use them the same way.

Anyone posting the same content across platforms uses this to cut an Instagram tag block down to something that fits Facebook, which usually means keeping two. Our [caption formatter](/tools/caption-formatter/) handles the line breaks, and the [general hashtag generator](/tools/hashtag-generator/) covers every platform in one place if you are adapting one message across several.

faqs.q: Do hashtags work on Facebook at all?
faqs.a: Barely. They are clickable and there are hashtag pages, but almost nobody browses them, and Facebook's reach comes from friends, groups and shares rather than subject tags. Two or three relevant ones are fine; expecting them to drive reach is not realistic.

Two or three. There is no benefit to more, and a long block makes the post look copied from another platform, which is not the impression you want in a feed full of posts from people someone actually knows.

faqs.q: What works better than hashtags on Facebook?
faqs.a: The first line of your text, because it decides whether anyone taps to expand. Posting into relevant groups, which reaches people who chose that subject. And anything that earns comments early, since conversation travels much further than likes.

faqs.q: Should I copy my Instagram caption across?
faqs.a: Not with the hashtags attached. The text usually transfers fine, but a thirty tag block is immediately recognisable as a copy and paste and reads badly on Facebook.

faqs.q: Do hashtags help in Facebook groups?
faqs.a: Slightly, because some groups use them to organise topics and members search within the group. Check whether the group has a convention before adding them; many do.
